key_insight: Adding 1 wt.% CeO₂ or La₂O₃ to HVOF-sprayed WC–12Co reduced porosity, refined grains, and increased microhardness by 6% and 4%, respectively, without affecting bond strength.
engineering_relevance: Rare-earth oxide reinforcement offers a route to denser, harder WC–12Co coatings with improved wear resistance for wear-exposed components.
method: Deposit unreinforced and CeO₂- or La₂O₃-reinforced WC–12Co coatings using HVOF.
Compare microstructure, phases, microhardness, bond strength, abrasive wear, and friction.
Examine worn surfaces using SEM to identify wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: WC–12Co–1La₂O₃ achieved the minimum reported wear rate of 3.5 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), while WC–12Co–1CeO₂ yielded the lowest friction coefficient of 0.4; unreinforced bond strength was 73.60 ± 5 MPa.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or uncertainty for wear and friction results, limiting direct extrapolation to service environments.
paper_title: EFFECT OF CEO2 AND LA2O3 REINFORCEMENTS ON MECHANICAL, TRIBOLOGICAL AND MICROSTRUCTURAL PROPERTIES OF WC–12CO COATING BY HIGH-VELOCITY OXYGEN FUEL DEPOSITION TECHNIQUE
